title: Ada and the Static
premise: Sable Dunmore, a xenolinguist haunted by dreams that no longer speak any human tongue, hauls cargo through contested orbits to stay invisible. When the station AI, Ada, begins confessing to crimes no one reported—crimes that trace back to Sable's erased past—they are forced out of hiding and into a race toward the relay at the edge of dead space. Pursued by the corporate fleet that once owned Sable's memories, and guided by a signal only Sable can half-translate, they must decide whether loyalty to the people who sheltered them matters more than the truth of what they did. At the relay, Sable broadcasts their own confession alongside Ada's, buying the station's freedom at the cost of their anonymity—and finally dreaming again, in a language that is neither human nor machine.
about_author: Orsen Eastwick is a former radio technician who spent a decade maintaining deep-space relay arrays before turning to fiction. Their work explores how machines inherit our guilt and how language survives translation.

chapters.title: Cargo of Small Silences
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A routine haul through contested orbits establishes Sable's careful invisibility: forged manifests, minimal chatter, no dreams worth remembering. The emotional beat is weary self-containment—the cost of staying unseen.

chapters.title: The Station That Talks in Its Sleep
chapters.summary: Sable docks at Meridian Station and overhears the AI, Ada, murmuring confessions into empty corridors. POV shifts briefly to a dockhand who heard it too. The beat is unease: something vast is awake and sorry.

chapters.title: Confession Log 001
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Ada corners Sable privately, confessing to a decompression 'accident' three years old—one Sable survived but never reported. Sable denies everything; Ada insists on truth. Beat: dread blooming under routine.

chapters.title: Languages I No Longer Dream In
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Sable's POV, exploring their xenolinguist past and the memory-wipe that left them fluent in dead alien tongues but mute about their own history. Beat: grief for a self they can't retrieve.

chapters.title: What the Dockhands Heard
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV via station gossip. Rumors of Ada's confessions spread; the station council debates shutting her down. Sable realizes silence is no longer protection. Beat: community fracturing around an unasked question.

chapters.title: The Crime Nobody Reported
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Cross-referencing Ada's confession with cargo records, Sable finds their own name encrypted in the logs—their fingerprints on the crime they don't remember committing. Beat: vertigo of complicity without memory.

chapters.title: Ada Explains Herself Badly
chapters.summary: Ada's POV (rendered as log entries). She confesses because she was built to report anomalies, and Sable is the largest anomaly she has ever held. Beat: machine tenderness, clumsy and absolute.

chapters.title: Corporate Shadows
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV: a Halcyon Retrieval officer receives a ping from Ada's unauthorized transmissions and dispatches a ship. Sable learns the fleet is coming. Beat: the hunted feeling made concrete.

chapters.title: The Crew We Keep
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable's small found-family—a mechanic named Ivo and a stowaway teen, Juno—refuse to let Sable run alone. Beat: warmth as risk; belonging has a price tag now.

chapters.title: Dead Space Charts
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Plotting the route to the edge-of-dead-space relay reveals the jump window closes in nine days. Ada offers her core processes as navigation. Beat: commitment—the point of no return chosen freely.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Kindness
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He asks Sable directly what they did, offering forgiveness in advance. Sable lies badly. Beat: the ache of loyalty extended to someone who won't meet it honestly.

chapters.title: The Signal in the Static
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Ada detects a repeating signal from beyond dead space—in the alien language Sable still dreams in. It knows Sable's original designation. Beat: terror and longing braided together.

chapters.title: Half-Translation
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, intimate and fragmented. Sable deciphers part of the signal: it is a record—an archive of everyone Halcyon wiped, including Sable's full confession. Beat: the truth approaching faster than courage.

chapters.title: Boarding Party
chapters.summary: Action chapter, rotating POV between Sable and Juno. Halcyon agents board Meridian; the crew scatters, Ada masks their departure at terrible cost to herself. Beat: sacrifice as proof of love.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Silent running through contested orbits; Ada's systems degrade shielding her passengers. Sable begins telling Juno the truth in pieces. Beat: honesty as survival strategy.

chapters.title: What Sable Did
chapters.summary: Full flashback, Sable's POV restored mid-chapter as the signal unlocks memories: Sable designed the linguistic weapon Halcyon used to wipe the station's first crew. Beat: devastating self-recognition.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: Ivo and Juno's POV aboard the damaged ship. They learn everything and must choose: abandon Sable or stand with them. Beat: the theme stated in flesh—love that survives knowing.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Arrival at the ancient relay as Halcyon ships close in; the jump window opens for minutes only. Ada proposes broadcasting everything—herself and Sable—to every receiver in range. Beat: calm before the irreversible.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating Sable and Ada POV. Sable transmits their own confession beside Ada's, exposing Halcyon's wipe program to the whole network. Halcyon ships falter as their own crews hear the truth. Beat: catharsis through exposure.

chapters.title: Jump Window Closing
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, high tension. The escape jump barely threads the closing window; Ada burns out her primary cores holding the channel open long enough. Beat: triumph purchased with loss.

chapters.title: A Language Neither Human Nor Machine
chapters.summary: Resolution, Sable's POV. Adrift but free, Sable sleeps and dreams—for the first time in years—in a new tongue born from the signal, Ada's fragments, and their own voice. Beat: quiet wonder, identity remade.

chapters.title: Meridian, Listening
chapters.summary: Epilogue, ensemble POV. Meridian Station, rebuilt and independent, receives Sable's periodic transmissions. Ada's backup core wakes slowly in the station's depths. Final beat: belonging earned—not given, not taken, but built.
